ENTREPRENEURSHIP

Banh Miow Cafe

Co-Owner & Operator Feb – Aug 2026

I’d always wanted to open a little storefront. We’re foodies and love making Vietnamese food, so I decided to give it a try.

We didn’t have software in place. I used AI tools, mostly Claude, to build Square-integrated kiosk, recipe, inventory, and prep-forecasting tools for the people actually running the café.

The recipe app guided drink preparation without requiring staff to memorize every recipe. We documented the recipes and all the little details that go into running a boba shop.

I spent a month testing and refining the app to help onboard new hires.

  • For our 80+ item menu, the workflow cut initial training from weeks of memorization to several hours of guided practice, helping everyone prepare drinks consistently. Consistent drinks made for happy customers.

Veronica Canido

Senior Frontend Engineer | React & TypeScript

Florida · veronicacanido@gmail.com

LinkedIn · GitHub · Website

Summary

Frontend-focused Software Engineer with 6+ years building and shipping production React and TypeScript applications across cybersecurity, healthcare, and fintech. Owned complex, cross-functional product work from technical design through launch and iteration, including reusable component systems, data-heavy workflows, API integrations, testing, and accessibility. Former team lead who remained hands-on in development, code review, and mentoring.

Technical Skills

Frontend: JavaScript (ES6+), TypeScript, HTML, CSS, React, Redux, TanStack Query (React Query), React Router, React Hook Form, Material UI, AG Grid, amCharts, Figma

Backend & Data: Node.js, Express, Meteor, MongoDB, SQL, Supabase/PostgreSQL, REST APIs, Spring Boot (Java/Groovy)

Testing & Quality: Jest, React Testing Library, Vitest, Snyk, WCAG/ADA accessibility

Practices & Tools: Git, CI/CD (GitLab CI/CD, Jenkins, GitHub Actions), Postman, Swagger/OpenAPI, Agile/Scrum, code review, Jira, AI-assisted development (Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT/Codex)

Professional Experience

Fortress Information Security - Software Engineer / Team Lead

May 2022 - Feb 2026

  • Led a cross-functional team of frontend and backend engineers and QA through planning and releases while remaining a hands-on developer.
  • Owned the catalog interface for an AI Monitoring product from evolving requirements and technical design through MVP release in React, Node.js, and MongoDB, giving customers a way to manage and visualize thousands of SBOM components.
  • Built UI features for the first product demo that helped secure a U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) contract, contributing from spec planning and architecture through multiple sprints of high-stakes delivery.
  • Optimized data-heavy views, including amCharts map visualizations and data tables aggregating hundreds of thousands of records, by restructuring MongoDB queries to eliminate unnecessary lookups and cut load times.
  • Created the project's shared frontend foundation and a reusable MUI Data Grid compatible with legacy and new column configurations, supporting a company-wide move away from SlickGrid and establishing patterns adopted across teams.
  • Used Claude with project-context documentation to navigate an unfamiliar Python codebase, reproduce a release-blocking import failure across mismatched backports, restore omitted payload fields, and coordinate cross-team regression testing.
  • Partnered with Product and Design to shape incomplete Figma flows; documented use cases, test plans, edge cases, and release guidance so technical and nontechnical teams could review changes clearly.
JPMorgan Chase - Software Engineer (Junior to Associate)

Jun 2019 - May 2022

  • Built a client-facing healthcare application using React, Redux, TypeScript, and Spring Boot, enabling clients to process payments, onboard users, analyze data, and monitor internal processes; collaborated with Product and UX from Figma designs through monthly production releases.
  • Delivered a full-stack operations portal from the ground up using React, Material UI, and Spring Boot, later adopted in production by internal teams.
  • Worked with JPMorgan Chase's shared Material UI-based component library for internal web applications; applied standardized components, submitted fixes through fork-based pull requests, patched versioned releases, and raised upstream issues with the library team when product needs required shared support.
  • Implemented automated test suites with Jest and React Testing Library, maintaining at least 70% test coverage; supported Jenkins CI checks, remediated Snyk findings, and delivered 90%+ WCAG compliance.
  • Mentored incoming SEP engineers and interns through their first roles at the firm.

Entrepreneurial Experience

Banh Miow Cafe - Co-Owner & Operator

Feb 2026 - Aug 2026

  • Co-founded and operated a cafe, owning the customer experience and day-to-day decisions across staffing, inventory, vendors, and budgeting.
  • Used AI-assisted tools to rapidly build a full-stack Square-integrated kiosk, recipe, inventory, and prep-forecasting app; its recipe workflow cut initial training for an 80+ item menu from weeks to several hours. Vite, Vercel Functions, Supabase/PostgreSQL, Square API.

Projects

  • Neko Dancer 2.0 - Browser multiplayer rhythm game with chart authoring, PixiJS gameplay, WebSocket rooms, chat, and synchronized YouTube playback. React, TypeScript, PixiJS, Node.js, WebSockets, YouTube IFrame API. Play-room design case study.
  • Hop//Beat - Deployed, playable browser-based spatial rhythm game using webcam pose tracking to turn full-body movement into gameplay. React, TypeScript, Vite, MediaPipe Pose Landmarker, PixiJS. Play the game.

Likes

  • Home den, not a corporate office.
  • Big window onto the backyard.
  • A large tree with little acorns.
  • Lots of squirrels, lizards, snakes, and birds.
  • An occasional rabbit, raccoon, coyote, and opossums.
  • Warm acacia-like hardwood floors.
  • White walls and a centered window, with the backyard tree on the left.
  • Two desks side by side, with Levi at his own desk.
  • Lumi and Luci in the room, matching the approved kitten art.
  • Yard animals drawn closer to the storybook character style.

Dislikes

  • The earlier navy office, cubicles, and meeting room.
  • The den was too warm / peach-amber.
  • Semi-realistic yard animals that looked pasted on.
  • Two identical tuxedo cats instead of distinct Lumi and Luci.
